pr_title: Fix forward compatibility issue of URL safe signed Id
pr_body:
Fixes #53710 

This Pull Request has been created because making signed Id URL safe is not forward compatible and it causes issue during rollout. Old instances of the application which haven't been updated yet cannot verify newly created URL safe signed Ids.

### Detail

This Pull Request uses a secondary signed Id verifier as a fallback to ensure forward compatibility during rollout.

After a successful rollout of these changes, `Rails.application.config.active_record.url_safe_signed_id` can be set to `true` to disable the fallback.

### Todo
For the latest version `url_safe_signed_id` variable can be removed and make the signed Id URL safe by default.

issue_context.title: `ActiveRecord::Base.signed_id_verifier` not forward compatible from 7.1 to upward
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
I have created a [repository](https://github.com/beauraF/signed-id-bug-reproduction) with a [test](https://github.com/beauraF/signed-id-bug-reproduction/blob/main/test/models/user_test.rb) that reproduce the issue.

### Expected behavior
We are able to use a signed id generated with rails 7.2 in a process still running rails 7.1 without any issue.

### Actual behavior
Because of [this change](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/49507), signed id generated with rails 7.2 will crash with a `ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier::InvalidSignature: mismatched digest` if used in a process still running rails 7.1. Leading to errors during a rolling rollout of 7.1 to 7.2/8.0 upgrade or in case of rollback.

I can work on a fix to make rails 7.1 forward compatible, but is that something you are interested in as rails 7.1 does not receive bug fix anymore?

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.1.5 / 7.2.2
**Ruby version**: 3.3.6

I thought it would come down to the same thing. Processes with the flag set to false won't be able to read ids coming from processes with the flag set to true. Unless we introduce a verifier to generate and a verifier to verify?
Both format should be able to be deserailized regardless of the value of the flag.

I can confirm that the mentioned change is not forward compatible. Here are some details:

When url_safe is set to true, MessageVerifier uses two different methods to decode and encode:
```ruby
# lib/active_support/messages/codec.rb

def encode(data, url_safe: @url_safe)
  url_safe ? ::Base64.urlsafe_encode64(data, padding: false) : ::Base64.strict_encode64(data)
end

def decode(encoded, url_safe: @url_safe)
  url_safe ? ::Base64.urlsafe_decode64(encoded) : ::Base64.strict_decode64(encoded)
  ...
end
```

So during a rollout, new application instances use `::Base64.urlsafe_encode64(data, padding: false)` to encode, while the old instances still use `::Base64.strict_decode64(encoded)` to decode. This causes the old instances to break.

One possible solution is to use two different configurations for generating signed IDs and verifying signed IDs:
```ruby
signed_id_verifier = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new secret, digest: "SHA256", serializer: JSON, url_safe: true

signed_id_generator = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new secret, digest: "SHA256", serializer: JSON
```
and unify them again in the next major(?) version. Should I work on this fix?
@beauraF do you need help with that one?
I started, but haven't had much time lately, I should be able to have another look on Saturday
@byroot @beauraF Yesterday, I created a [merge request](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54290) to address this issue. Can I have your review on it?

I feel https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54290 is only half the fix though. It allow 7.2 to understand 7.1 generated messages, but when you rollout your upgrade, you have both versions running for a while.

So you also need some extra code to force 7.2+ to keep generating 7.1 style messages OR backport a feature to 7.1 to allow it to understand 7.2+ messages.

I’ve tried to elaborate on the solution. There are two versions of generating signed IDs:
- Version 1 (introduced in Rails 7.1): This uses a URL unsafe format.
- Version 2 (introduced in Rails 7.2): This uses a URL safe format and is backward compatible with version 1.

The issue arises because version 1 cannot understand IDs generated by version 2. Why does this matter? Let’s consider an application upgrading to Rails 7.2 (version 2). During the rollout, some instances might still be running version 1 (old), while others are using version 2 (new). If an old instance (with version 1) receives a signed ID generated by a new instance (with version 2), it won’t be able to decode the base64 format properly. This results in a forward compatibility issue.

**How does the solution work?**
- By default, url_safe_signed_id is set to false. This means signed IDs are generated using version 1 (URL unsafe format).
- The changes in [#54290](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54290) ensure that version 2 (URL safe) IDs can also be accepted, but they won’t generate URL safe IDs yet.
- We deploy the code with this change.
- After the first deployment, we can set url_safe_signed_id to true. This will start generating signed IDs in the URL safe format (version 2).
- We deploy again. Now, the old instances can verify signed IDs generated by the new instances.
